q: We present a specification-driven governance framework that treats the specification as the primary governance artifact and the shared contract for human–AI collaboration.
r: Include: specification-driven governance of AI-generated code with a spec review gate, approved baseline and a controlled human study (group a).

q: strict decoupling of pedagogical specification from implementation
r: Include: spec-first agentic coding workflow (specification, acceptance tests, approval gates) run with Claude Code, Codex and others, in three case studies (group a).

q: We conducted two studies comparing non-governed and governed AI-assisted development: bootstrapping a new project (Setup) and implementing a complex feature (Extension).
r: Include: schema and contract as source of truth with guardrails for coding agents, compared against a non-governed baseline on project and feature tasks (group a).

q: ACM, New York, NY, USA, 2 pages.
r: EC3: two-page ICSE-Companion vision paper with hypotheses and a research agenda, no agent evaluated.

q: shifts the developer’s focus from writing low-level code to designing high-level
r: Include: SysSpec specification-driven LLM code generation and evolution; this is the journal version, so the arXiv record rayyan-800486075 carries EC4 (group a).

q: This paper introduces command coding, a structured methodology that applies traditional software engineering management principles
r: Include: plan-and-review methodology for orchestrating coding agents, related to SDD, with a production case study measuring effort and quality (group a).

q: Formal verification avoids both problems, but existing work covers only standalone tasks whose specifications are given as input, not real issues
r: EC6: SWE-bench-style issue repair benchmark (SWE-Proof), always excluded.

q: ReqClarifyBench: We introduce ReqClarifyBench, the first interactive requirement clarification benchmark for repository-level software development
r: EC6: the evaluated task is requirement clarification into a document, not writing or changing code.

q: natural-language code documentation that describes the behavior of program entities and guides agents in generating correct code
r: Include: behavioural specifications as optimised external context for coding agents, tested on new-feature and translation tasks (group b, so EC5 does not apply).

q: We define Gauntlet’s trajectory-similarity and build-gated scores, attack-success estimators, Wilson intervals, and case-cluster bootstrap summaries.
r: Include: a large part of the contribution is an evaluation protocol with new scores, bootstrap intervals and raw-versus-governed comparison on application briefs (EC6 ii); borderline against EC5.
